transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ben Wallace (Redwood SE), Evan Stone (Nimbus CTO), Leila Moore (Nimbus ML Eng), Marcus Liu (Nimbus Infra)

Auto-summary: Quick parity demo showing how existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls map to Redwood endpoints, console walkthrough for routing and rollouts, plus Optimize recommendations. Questions about latency, cost, and VPC. Next: send parity doc, run pilot benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood. Can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Evan Stone: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Alex.
[00:07] Leila Moore: Yep good.
[00:10] Alex Chen: Cool. Quick intro \u0014 I'm Alex (AE) with Redwood, Priya and Ben who will walk through the migration parity and some perf bits. Evan, Leila, Marcus \u0014 do you want to intro real quick?
[00:20] Evan Stone: Sure. I'm Evan, CTO at Nimbus. We run a conversational product and we've been on OpenAI for gen and Together for some LLM workloads. Leila owns model infra and Marcus is infra.
[00:30] Marcus Liu: Hi all. We'll mostly be asking about latency and VPC options.
[00:34] Priya Nair: Great \u0014 the plan: quick API parity mapping, Console demo for routing and rollouts, then Optimize (batching/cache) and QA.

[01:02] Priya Nair: Ok starting with API parity. Redwood exposes a single REST endpoint /v1/generate and /v1/chat and embeddings endpoint and supports the common parameters you expect \u0014 temperature, max_tokens, top_p, stop sequences, streaming, and also function-calling. So from OpenAI calls you can map engine/model to Redwood
[01:22] Leila Moore: How exact is the function-calling parity? We use structured output heavily.
[01:27] Ben Wallace: We support both OpenAI style function call payloads and a JSON-schema-driven structured output. There are small differences \u0014 e.g. our response contains model_profile and route_id in the metadata which sometimes trips up strict SDKs, but we provide prebuilt client helpers.
[01:45] Evan Stone: And Together/Anthropic tokens or params \u0014 top_p equivalents?
[01:50] Priya Nair: Yes, top_p present. For Anthropic there are different sampling defaults, but you can set temp/top_p/presence_penalty. We showed a parity spreadsheet in the deck \u0014 it lists param equivalences: e.g. anthropic 'max_tokens_to_sample' -> Redwood 'max_tokens'. Sometimes parameter names differ but semantics map 1:1.

[02:30] Marcus Liu: What about streaming? We need token streaming for live chat.
[02:34] Ben Wallace: Streaming supported. We have SSE and websocket options. Streaming behavior aims to match OpenAI's chunked token delivery. There might be micro-diffs in chunk boundaries but RFC-level behavior is same.

[03:15] Leila Moore: Embeddings \u0014 we use OpenAI embeddings and Together for semantic search. Anything special to know?
[03:20] Priya Nair: Redwood supports several embeddings model variants. The output vector dims are model dependent and we list mapping rules in the parity doc. We also include a migration helper script that normalizes distances if you switch vector dims \u0014 or you can pin to a matching Redwood-verified model that matches OpenAI's vector size.
[03:45] Leila Moore: Ok \u0014 good. We have a vector DB so we need stable dims or reindex.

[04:05] Evan Stone: Cost comparisons \u0014 can you give rough delta when moving from OpenAI to Redwood hosted?
[04:12] Alex Chen: We'll provide a cost worksheet. In practice you see cost changes driven by batching and quantization \u0014 Redwood Optimize recommendations often reduce per-token cost by 20-40% depending on workload. But exact numbers depend on token mix, streaming vs non-streaming, and whether you use Dedicated. We'll run benchmarks during the pilot.

[05:00] Priya Nair: Now Console \u0014 I'll share my screen. (screen share) All right you can see the Redwood Console, top-left is the model catalog. You can pin model versions to routes, configure canary rollouts, and set policy-based routing (latency-first or cost-first).
[05:22] Evan Stone: Can routes be per-API-key? We have tenant-level keys.
[05:26] Priya Nair: Yes, routes are per project and you can create API-key scoped routes. RBAC ties into SSO.

[06:05] Priya Nair: Demonstrating a route that splits 5% canary to a newer quantized variant; if errors spike we automatically fallback to the previous model. We also show request tracing \u0014 token-level latency, cost breakdown, and KV cache hit rates.
[06:25] Marcus Liu: KV cache? You mean prefix cache for chat?
[06:28] Ben Wallace: Exactly \u0014 prefix/KV caching for conversation context. We show cache hit %, which can dramatically reduce tokens billed on upstream.

[07:00] Leila Moore: How about rollout audit logs for compliance?
[07:03] Priya Nair: Full audit logs \u0014 model rollouts, config changes, API key usage. We integrate with your SIEM via log export. Also support KMS for customer-managed keys.

[07:35] Evan Stone: We need SOC2 and legal docs.
[07:38] Alex Chen: We'll share the SOC2 package link. Redwood is SOC2 Type II (we have docs and a data processing addendum).

[08:10] Priya Nair: On deployments: three modes \u0014 Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private (VPC/on-prem). For strict data residency or air-gapped needs we support private deployments with a local control plane.
[08:30] Marcus Liu: For the pilot we want hosted but with VPC peering or Private link. Is that supported?
[08:35] Ben Wallace: Yes \u0014 VPC peering, PrivateLink and customer-managed KMS are available for Dedicated and Private, and for Hosted we offer VPC peering options for enterprise accounts.

[09:05] Evan Stone: Latency \u0014 what's the p95 for text generation?
[09:10] Priya Nair: It varies by model and length. For a typical chat (1-2 prompt turns) p95 can be 200-400ms on our optimized small models; larger LLMs will be higher. We'll run a benchmark against your prompts to provide realistic numbers.

[10:00] Leila Moore: Quantization \u0014 do you support int8/4 for LLMs and how does that affect quality?
[10:05] Ben Wallace: Yes, we support multiple quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization by workload; it simulates quality delta using your eval prompts and flags regressions \u0014 you can then pin models per route. Quality usually drops minimally for many tasks at int8, but depends on model.

[11:10] Evan Stone: Ok show us an example API call mapping from OpenAI to Redwood?
[11:15] Priya Nair: Sure. OpenAI chat completion POST to /v1/chat/completions with model:gpt-4o-openai, messages, temperature, functions \u0014 on Redwood you'd POST /v1/chat with model:"redwood/gpt-4o-compat" (or one of our compatibility aliases), include the same messages and functions block. Response schema is similar but note metadata field names.
[11:40] Leila Moore: Will current SDKs break? We have internal wrappers.
[11:45] Alex Chen: We provide client SDK migrations \u0014 a shim layer that translates OpenAI-style requests to Redwood and vice versa. For most teams it's a config change + minor shim. We'll include code snippets in the migration guide.

[12:35] Priya Nair: Here's the parity spreadsheet \u0014 shows param mapping for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood. For example Together's 'sampling_params' map into Redwood 'temperature/top_p/typical_p' depending on flavor.

[13:10] Marcus Liu: How do we handle model version pinning for safety/regulation?
[13:14] Ben Wallace: You can pin exact model builds and put them behind a route that only certain API keys can access. We retain model provenance in audit logs for compliance.

[14:00] Leila Moore: A couple of gotchas we've had: stop-token behavior differs slightly across vendors and causes truncation issues. Any notes?
[14:08] Priya Nair: Yep, stop behavior can differ. We recommend a brief compatibility test suite (we can share one). For stop tokens we replicate common behaviors and document edgecases in the parity doc.

[15:00] Evan Stone: Security question \u0014 data retention. We want no retention for PII.
[15:05] Alex Chen: You can opt-out of telemetry and set retention to 0 for customer data on Private and Dedicated; on Hosted we offer retention controls and data deletion/retention agreements for enterprise tiers. We'll include the DPA language.

[16:00] Priya Nair: Now Optimize \u0014 this is our cost/perf toolkit. It analyzes traces, suggests batching sizes, caching rules, and quantization profiles. Example: for high-throughput short prompts it suggested a 64-request batch and enabled prefix caching which reduced tokens by 30% and improved effective throughput.

[16:35] Leila Moore: Does Optimize run on our data or only aggregate telemetry?
[16:40] Ben Wallace: Optimize runs on metadata and optional traces; you can opt-in per project. For privacy-focused customers we run it in your VPC when on Private.

[17:10] Evan Stone: For embeddings pipeline \u0014 can Optimize recommend model/quantization for index-time vs query-time?
[17:16] Priya Nair: Yes. It will recommend heavier quantization at index-time (retrade for storage) and a higher-quality model at query-time if you need precision. Also suggests reindex windows based on traffic.

[18:00] Marcus Liu: Pilot: we want a small pilot with 10k requests/day and compare latency/cost to OpenAI.
[18:05] Alex Chen: Great \u0014 we'll provision a pilot project. Priya will run a benchmark harness that replays your sample traffic and returns p50/p95/p99 and cost-estimated.

[19:20] Priya Nair: I'll share the benchmark template. It supports streaming, non-streaming, embeddings, and function-call tests. For fairness we run the same prompt set and tokenization.

[20:00] Leila Moore: On the legal/procurement side we have standard security questionnaire.
[20:05] Alex Chen: Send it over to me and I'll loop in security; we'll respond within 48 hours for standard items, and we have a security pack for enterprise.

[21:00] Evan Stone: Any differences in rate limiting or quotas? We use burst traffic occasionally.

[21:05] Ben Wallace: We support burst capacity policies for Dedicated/reserved, and adaptive token-level rate limits on Hosted. We can set per-route throttles and provide client-side retry guidance.

[22:00] Leila Moore: Does Redwood expose kernel-level perf tuning or do we see that only in Dedicated?

[22:05] Priya Nair: Kernel selection is internal to our runtime; Dedicated gives you more determinism because you have reserved GPU pools, but the same optimizations apply in Hosted. For deterministic latency we usually recommend Dedicated.

[23:10] Evan Stone: Example of a migration code snippet?
[23:15] Alex Chen: (shares snippet) Example Node shim: replace openai.Completion.create(...) with redwood.client.chat.create(...) or use our compatibility shim that accepts openai-style args. We'll send this in the migration guide.

[24:00] Leila Moore: What about tooling integration \u0014 Datadog/Prometheus?

[24:04] Ben Wallace: We have metrics exports, traces, and logs. Datadog and Prometheus integrations are supported and you can ingest tracing via open-telemetry.

[25:00] Marcus Liu: Is there non-repudiation for logs? We need immutable logs for audits.

[25:05] Priya Nair: Audit logs can be exported to append-only buckets and integrated with your SIEM; we also support signed event logs in Private deployments.

[26:30] Alex Chen: Quick interlude \u0014 any blockers we haven't covered?
[26:35] Evan Stone: Main ones are latency parity, cost delta, and legal \u0014 SOC2 + DPA. Also embeddings vector dims and reindexing effort.

[27:20] Priya Nair: We'll provide the parity spreadsheet, SDK shim, and a pilot proposal for the benchmark. The pilot will include a replay of 10k/day for 7 days and we'll return p50/p95/p99 and cost delta.

[28:15] Leila Moore: About function calls and structured outputs \u0014 do you preserve function-name ordering and call metadata?

[28:20] Ben Wallace: Yes, function call metadata included; we include confidence signals in the metadata. Small differences may exist in how ambiguous calls are handled but we can tune via evals.

[29:10] Evan Stone: Is there a way to auto-fallback to OpenAI if Redwood route fails?

[29:15] Alex Chen: Yes, policy-based fallback to compatible upstream (OpenAI or another variant) is supported \u0014 we call that multi-tier routing, useful during migrations.

[30:00] Priya Nair: Walkthrough of the Optimize UI \u0014 shows recommended batch size, cache rules, and expected cost delta. You can accept a recommendation and apply it to a route. It also shows historical regressions so you can rollback.

[31:10] Marcus Liu: For our compliance we need contract language around customer keys and KMS.

[31:15] Alex Chen: We'll include the KMS integration docs and a sample DPA clause.

[32:00] Leila Moore: Ok, curious \u0014 how long does a typical migration take? Weekslines?

[32:05] Priya Nair: Typical timeline: PoC/benchmark 2 weeks, pilot 2-4 weeks, full migration depends on reindexing and integration. For you, since you have both gen and embeddings, I'd estimate 4-8 weeks to roll to prod with an overlap/fallback strategy.

[33:10] Evan Stone: That works. Our procurement lead will need cost estimates.

[34:00] Alex Chen: We'll include a pricing worksheet based on 100k req/day and your token mix. Also show Dedicated pricing if you want stable latency.

[35:00] Leila Moore: Anything else on developer ergonomics?

[35:05] Ben Wallace: We have SDKs in Node/Python/Go, and the compatibility shim reduces code changes. We also provide CLI tools for model pulls and tests.

[36:20] Marcus Liu: Do you provide hooks for feature flagging per route?

[36:24] Priya Nair: Yes, route-level feature flags and A/B testing built-in in Console.

[37:30] Evan Stone: For the pilot we'll need a non-prod project with same quota and a runbook for the benchmark.

[37:35] Alex Chen: We'll provision that. Priya, Ben will own the runbook.

[38:00] Priya Nair: I'll send the runbook and the parity spreadsheet after the call. The runbook includes the benchmark harness and notes for streaming tests.

[39:40] Leila Moore: If we find quality regressions, what's the rollback latency?

[39:45] Ben Wallace: Rollback is immediate \u0014 we flip the route and traffic returns to previous model. You can also do partial traffic percentages for canarying.

[40:30] Evan Stone: Any SLA for hosted?

[40:33] Alex Chen: Hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime/latency targets depending on contract.

[41:20] Marcus Liu: For logs retention policy \u0014 how long do you keep logs by default?

[41:25] Priya Nair: Default 30 days for Hosted but enterprise tiers can extend or we can export to customer bucket for long-term retention.

[42:10] Evan Stone: Great. Let's confirm next steps and owners.

[42:15] Alex Chen: Recap \u0014 Alex will send parity mapping doc, SDK migration guide, SOC2/security pack, and pricing worksheet. Priya will schedule the pilot and share benchmark runbook. Nimbus team will share prompt set and traffic profile.

[43:05] Evan Stone: Sounds good. We'll aim to send the prompt set by Thursday.

[43:20] Leila Moore: Quick question on function call telemetry \u0014 do you log full function args? We prefer redaction.

[43:25] Ben Wallace: You can opt to redact/obfuscate arguments in logs and in Optimize. Defaults are to not log PII.

[44:00] Alex Chen: Any final Qs?

[44:05] Marcus Liu: No, that's it.

[44:10] Evan Stone: Thanks everyone.

[44:12] Alex Chen: Thanks all \u0014 we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[44:20] Priya Nair: I'll shoot calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.

[44:30] Ben Wallace: Thanks.

[44:40] End meeting notes: Action items captured above. Follow-ups: parity doc, SDK guide, SOC2 pack, pilot runbook, sample prompt set.

(Transcript may contain minor transcription errors and mis-attributions.)
